This route takes the course on the EU-frames case for a reader who works alone, without a facilitator and without a class, in five stages and at your own pace. The case is a study of sixteen waves of the Eurobarometer, which asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the member states frame the European Union, and its claim is one made by the original author (OA) [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic] that five analysts reanalysed in the Multi100 project. The modules of the [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) sit between the tasks of the exercise, each at the point where the case first needs its method, from the panel of country-years that you build yourself from the survey files to fixed effects with few clusters and a curve of 864 specifications. The route ends on a project of your own. A semester course can take the same route in class.

You leave with a case report and a project of your own. The report contains the estimand statement and the causal graph of the claim, the reproduction of a recorded result, your exploration of the menu, a preregistration completed before its specification ran, and the result of that specification with its place on the curve of the claim. The project asks a question beyond the claim, preregistered before it ran. Both sit in a version-controlled repository that another person can clone and re-render, with the licensed survey files left out of it, as the terms of their archive require.

## How you work

No programming is assumed. Stage 1 installs R, Quarto, an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) and the downloadable workspace of the case, which holds the country-year panel, the code of the tasks and the report that you fill in, and stage 2 teaches enough R to start the case. You work in the workspace on your own machine. The browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, holds every task as well, with hints and worked solutions, and it carries the work if your installation fails. Stage 3 offers to rebuild the panel from the sixteen Eurobarometer files from which it was made, which the GESIS archive distributes under a free account. The download is optional, and the stage says what to do without it.

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The exercise runs through five tasks. Task 1 is the setup check, Task 2 meets the panel, writes the estimand statement and finishes the causal graph, and Task 3 reproduces a result that Multi100 recorded for one of the five analysts. Task 4 explores the specification menu one decision at a time, and Task 5 declares one specification in a short preregistration, runs it and reports it. Stage 1 takes Task 1, stage 3 Tasks 2 and 3, and stage 4 Tasks 4 and 5.

Each stage has a page that lists its steps in order, and each step has a button that opens the page or the section where the work is done. Nothing in it depends on a pace, so a stage can be taken in one sitting or spread over a week. Where a stage can be shortened for a reader who already knows part of its material, its page says how, in a paragraph headed **Shortcuts**.

Without a facilitator, the checks are built into the pages. Each stage names the numbers that your code should reach, the browser lab holds hints and worked solutions for the tasks, and the [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. The stages use the full deck of the case, which includes every optional run of slides. Open it in its own tab and press `s` for the speaker view, whose notes give what is said over each slide, and where a slide asks the class to write something and send it together, write it into your report instead.

Sending your results to the class chart of the case is optional. A result sent alone joins the chart on the [Multiverse page](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#class-results), beside the results that earlier cohorts sent, and the helpers of Tasks 4 and 5 work exactly as they do in the one-day workshop: `submit_exploration()` and `report_result()` fill in the results form for you. To find your own marks again, give the same nickname every time, as `nickname = "..."`.

## The stages

| Stage | What you do | Time |
|---|---|---:|
| [Stage 1 – Credibility and the three Rs](stage-1.qmd) | Why the field talks of a crisis, reproduction, robustness and replication, SCORE and Multi100, and R, Quarto, an IDE and the workspace installed | 5 h 15 |
| [Stage 2 – R and Quarto](stage-2.qmd) | A first session in R, R on the panel of the case, the document format of the report, and the paper with the first sections of the case study | 5 h 50 |
| [Stage 3 – From respondents to a panel](stage-3.qmd) | Sixteen Eurobarometer files turned into country-years, the estimand statement and the causal graph, a recorded result reproduced, and the models of a panel | 6 h 45 |
| [Stage 4 – Few clusters and the multiverse](stage-4.qmd) | Tasks 4 and 5 on the curve of 864, inference with 27 countries, the multiverse and its critics, missing answers, the case report and the choice of a project | 6 h 35 |
| [Stage 5 – Your own project](stage-5.qmd) | Version control, a question beyond the claim, preregistered before it runs, and a repository ready for an archive | 6 h 15 |
| The route | | 30 h 40 |

[Start with Stage 1](stage-1.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The same case is also taught with a facilitator, as the [one-day workshop](../eu-frames-one-day/index.qmd) and as the [Extended course](../eu-frames-extended/index.qmd), whose third day takes the respondents within the panel.
